obligations.summary: Providers of high-risk AI systems placed on the Union market must report any serious incident to the market surveillance authorities of the Member States where the incident occurred.

The serious incident report must be made immediately after a causal link (or reasonable likelihood thereof) is established, and in any event no later than 15 days after the provider or deployer becomes aware of the serious incident, taking into account severity.
exceptions: Timelines may vary depending on the severity of the incident
Deployer awareness triggers the timeline where applicable

obligations.summary: In the event of a widespread infringement or a serious incident as defined in Article 3(49)(b), the provider or deployer must report immediately and no later than two days after becoming aware of the incident.

In the event of the death of a person, the provider or deployer must report immediately after establishing or suspecting a causal relationship between the high-risk AI system and the incident, but no later than 10 days after becoming aware of it.
Where necessary to ensure timely reporting, the provider or deployer may submit an initial incomplete report followed by a complete report.
Following the reporting of a serious incident, the provider must without delay perform necessary investigations including a risk assessment and corrective action.

The provider must cooperate with competent authorities and, where relevant, the notified body during investigations, and must not alter the AI system in a way that may affect evaluation of the causes without first informing competent authorities.

Upon receiving a notification related to a serious incident as defined in Article 3(49)(c), the relevant market surveillance authority must inform the national public authorities or bodies referred to in Article 77(1).
The Commission must develop dedicated guidance to facilitate compliance with the serious incident reporting obligations, to be issued by 2 August 2025 and assessed regularly.

Market surveillance authorities must take appropriate measures within seven days of receiving a serious incident notification and follow the notification procedures provided in Regulation (EU) 2019/1020.
For high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III placed by providers subject to equivalent Union reporting obligations, serious incident notifications are limited to those defined in Article 3(49)(c).
exceptions: Notification scope is limited to Article 3(49)(c) incidents where providers are already subject to equivalent Union legislative reporting obligations

obligations.summary: For high-risk AI systems that are safety components or devices covered by Regulations (EU) 2017/745 and 2017/746, serious incident notifications are limited to those defined in Article 3(49)(c) and must be made to the national competent authority designated by the Member State where the incident occurred.
exceptions: Notification scope is limited to Article 3(49)(c) incidents for devices covered by Regulations (EU) 2017/745 and 2017/746

obligations.summary: National competent authorities must immediately notify the Commission of any serious incident, whether or not action has been taken, in accordance with Article 20 of Regulation (EU) 2019/1020.
